Stated Claim / Post Context:
Fancy bars, bulk parking: Inside this agency's $5.9 million office move

It's their second office move in less than a decade, courtesy of the taxpayer.

Actual Article Body:
Your digital subscription includes access to content from all our websites in your region.
Access unlimited news content and The Canberra Times app. Premium subscribers also enjoy interactive puzzles and access to the digital version of our print edition - Today's Paper.

Picture this: you move into a brand new office at the lively end of Civic, with views over the lake and ample public parking.

Login or signup to continue reading

It's an elevator ride to four-star-plus restobars like Mu, Karl's Bar, and the Meat and Wine Co.

What's the catch?

The move will cost the taxpayer $5.9 million for the fitout alone, Austender records have revealed.

About 250 staff from federal agency Austrade will move into a new building on the corner of Constitution Avenue and London Circuit in 2027.

Chandeliers in the lobby and floor-to-ceiling glass windows will greet agency staff at Vernon, developed by Capital Property Group, with other features like an events space.

It has raised questions about value for money for the taxpayer, at a time when the government is looking for savings.

Agents say building moves can cost the equivalent of two to three years of rent, and Austrade staff have already moved office once in the past decade.

The per-head lease cost at Vernon - $11,400 a year - is well above the federal government benchmark for its agencies of $8500.

Rents on new office floors in Civic are typically 20 to 30 per cent more expensive than existing floors, many of which are sitting idle.

On the other hand, officials say the rent bill at Vernon will be cheaper than Austrade's current building at NewActon.

"Austrade conducted a full open market tender process, which included extensive negotiations with multiple prospective landlords," an agency source said.

"Following these negotiations, Austrade entered into a lease with Canberra Airport Group and was able to achieve better than market expectations, providing value for money for the taxpayer."

Austrade last moved office in the late 2010s, during a Coalition government bid to fill unused government office space.

The move out of the Nishi building will put Austrade staff in the same precinct as law and consulting firms Mallesons, MinterEllison, and Ernst & Young.

Jones Lang LaSalle is the leasing agent at Vernon, and its own Canberra staff will move into the building in February 2027.
